# Hustl

> Hustl is a self-hosted invoicing and finance app for freelancers and small studios. It runs on your own server, with no cloud account and no telemetry in the app.

## Canonical pages

- English: https://bitm4ncer.github.io/hustl/
- German: https://bitm4ncer.github.io/hustl/de/
- Source: https://github.com/bitm4ncer/hustl
- Documentation: https://github.com/bitm4ncer/hustl#readme
- German documentation: https://github.com/bitm4ncer/hustl/blob/main/README.de.md
- Installation with an agent: https://github.com/bitm4ncer/hustl/blob/main/INSTALL-WITH-AGENT.md
- Latest release: https://github.com/bitm4ncer/hustl/releases/latest
- License: https://github.com/bitm4ncer/hustl/blob/main/LICENSE (ISC)

## What it does

- Invoices, sequential numbering, PDF export and e-invoices according to EN 16931 (ZUGFeRD / Factur-X)
- Offers with versions, status and PDF
- Clients and projects with hours, fixed prices and open items
- Finance dashboard with income, expenses, fixed costs, forecast and monthly export
- Receipt PDFs, bank statement import and payment matching
- Planner with dated tasks, recurring routines and free lists, German/English UI, 12 currencies and a full archive

## Hosting

The recommended setup is a Debian/Ubuntu VPS with Docker and a domain. The installer sets up Docker, HTTPS in bundled mode, a daily database snapshot and autostart. Alternatives: an existing Linux server or NAS with Docker, a Raspberry Pi/home server, or a PaaS/Kubernetes environment with a persistent block volume and one replica. Shared hosting and serverless platforms without persistent storage are not suitable. The desktop app is a shell around a reachable server URL, not a standalone server.

## Requirements

- Linux host with Docker and persistent storage
- 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM minimum, 4 GB recommended
- 20 GB disk recommended
- Domain with an A record (AAAA for IPv6)
- About 15–30 minutes for the first build, plus DNS propagation

## Not included

SMTP email sending, GoCardless bank sync and Notion import are not part of the current release. The app is designed for one person per instance; multiple passkeys and devices are supported, but there are no roles or teams.
